description:
Continuation of the landed-on-branch fz-k22.18/.14/.20 work (branch fz-k22.18/callable-entry-ownership @ f557a9c7d, evaluated 2026-07-11: architecture adopted; lib 1330/0/6; fz-pcd FIXED 10/2; enum_predicate_search::interp GREEN; actor_ring::interp GREEN; matrix delta 74->75). TWO blockers before fold:

1. REGRESSION (blocking): resource_index_payload_private::{run,build} HANGS (30s timeout, output stalls after nil) -- previously green. Not a clean diagnostic: likely a WRONG entry stamped for a position (or a mis-split capture prefix for the 1-published-lane-over-0-param body this fixture exercises -- the same benign-superset shape that false-fired the k22.19 registry variant) causing a runtime livelock. Root-cause first; never-worse-than-clean-crash is the branch standard.

2. UNSTAMPED ENTRIES: materialize_callable_entry_positions (jobs/backend.rs) stamps a position only on an EXACTLY-ONE entry match and silently skips multi-matches -- precisely the multi-resolution callables this epic exists for. Downstream clean errors: enum_predicate_search::run "closure call target 48 disagrees with resolved entry 0 target 47"; enum_take_drop_split::run "materialize direct-only callable CallableId(19) without its upstream resolved entry"; ::interp "no resolved entry identity or direct target". FIX: per-position disambiguation -- the positions own demand context (its executable/clause origin, its position shapes grounded surface) selects WHICH resolution; a position that genuinely reaches N resolutions needs N-aware handling (the entry identity is per-resolution; the position knows its grounding). Both blockers are likely the same root (position->entry mapping correctness).

ACCEPTANCE: resource_index_payload_private green again; enum_predicate_search + enum_take_drop_split green on run/interp/build (the epics goal); matrix name-set vs eae19c725 baseline shows ONLY removals (actor_ring::interp stays fixed, nothing new red); lib/clippy green; determinism retained (byte-identical repeat runs). Work on branch wt/k22-20-finish (based at f557a9c7d).

comments.text:
BLOCKER 1 ROOT-CAUSED (investigation pass, no fix landed, worktree clean at f557a9c7d). NOT the packaging split (probe: CallableId(0)=R.drop/1, capture_lanes=0, target param_reprs=0, split 0/0 clean). ACTUAL: emit_drain_dtor_entry (native_codegen/driver.rs:387-432) hardcodes the 1-arg resource-dtor calling convention (payload_ref, closure, halt_cl); R.drop(_) ignores its arg -> demand elision compiles the body with 0 params. The boundary publishes 1 arg lane (its contract, transport.rs:3966-3978) but NOTHING propagates boundary-required INPUT demand into the resolved target's input_demands -- only the RETURN side has that pin (callable_boundary_return_demand_contributions_product, runtime_demand.rs:1031-1069, called from derive_member_demand :673-674). Runtime: call_indirect under a mismatched sig -> same closure ref invoked forever (verified via fz_closure_code_ref probe + sample stack).

WHY THE NEW MODEL EXPOSED IT: old model declared sigs from the boundary surface (1 lane) so the shim's 1-arg call matched and the 0-param body ignored the extra (the k22.19 benign-superset evidence). New model makes the target's compiled ABI authoritative -> shim mismatches. The boundary-surface-as-contract was never enforced on the body's demand.

FIX DESIGN (model-level, to implement): sibling callable_boundary_INPUT_demand_contributions_product -- for each flow.first_class_surfaces entry, join a boundary_runtime_demand-style non-Ignore demand into each resolution's input_demands[semantic_index] for the surface's argument positions (mirror boundary_lanes_for_shape/boundary_runtime_demand from the return side), threaded through the same fixpoint round (runtime_demand.rs:673-681). Requires making the contributions channel position-aware: HashMap<ExecutableKey, RuntimeDemand> (single return slot) -> keyed per arg position, e.g. HashMap<(ExecutableKey, usize), RuntimeDemand>. GENERAL: any boundary-published callable with elided params breaks the same way under entry-ownership; this closes the class. Monotone: joining non-Ignore demand is a widening in the demand lattice's ascent direction (same as the return pin) -- verify against unknown-is-not-none.

BLOCKER 2 (unexamined this pass): materialize_callable_entry_positions per-position disambiguation (backend.rs:471-531).

TASK 1 LANDED on wt/k22-20-finish @ cdd5cb572 (audit next, then fold): callable_boundary_input_demand_contributions_product mirroring the return side, per-position TargetDemandContribution channel, join_previous_input_demands (input_demands were rebuilt from scratch each round -- latent gap), cross-cone replace_settled_input_demand_contributions/recompute_input_demand siblings. emit_drain_dtor_entry needed NO change. resource_index_payload_private green all legs; actor_ring fully clean (its interp flake was the hang); matrix 73 vs 74 baseline = one removal zero new red; lib 1330/0/6; clippy clean; 5+ run determinism. TASK 2 -> split to fz-k22.23 (position-level disambiguation proven impossible; value-carried-identity dispatch is the fix). NOTE: repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2 matrix leg was red at f557a9c7d BASELINE too (spurious type/no-matching-clause warnings; the fz-pcd wrong-output core IS fixed, 10/2 correct) -- the warnings need a separate diagnosis.
